chunks: Then he (peace be upon him) said: After speaking another word: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father (peace be upon them), from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), that he said:
He who likened Him to His creation did not know Allah, and he who described Him with justice who attributed to Him the sins of His servants.
The hadith is long. We have taken from it the required passage. I have transmitted all of it in the commentary of the Qur'an.
ai.seo_question: How does knowing Allah involve avoiding anthropomorphism and attributing sins to Him?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the renowned Fourteen Infallibles, establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of *tanzih* (divine transcendence) by negating anthropomorphism (*tashbih*) and attributing human moral failings to Allah. It serves as a critical counter to the Mu'tazilite and Ash'ari debates on divine attributes, affirming that God's essence is utterly distinct from creation. Shaykh al-Saduq’s inclusion of this excerpt from his *Tafsir* highlights the interplay between creed and exegesis in early Shia scholarship.
